etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tremour (“fright”), from Anglo-Norman tremour and Old French tremor, from Latin tremor.

definitions.definition: (medicine) A rhythmic, uncontrollable shaking of all or part of the body due to partial muscle contractions.
To shake or quiver excessively and rapidly or involuntarily; to tremble.

quote.citation: 2004, Andrea Levy, chapter 17, in Small Island‎[1], London: Review, page 188:
quote.text: The ground tremored under their big boots.
